selection.diff_summary:
Summary: The change refactors Clang CodeGen’s handling of the implicit `this` parameter for constructors/destructors and other member-like calls so the ABI layer can choose the correct object type based on `GlobalDecl`, not just the method declaration. In the Microsoft ABI path, destructors now distinguish complete destructors from deleting/base destructors and use the vftable lookup for the appropriate destructor flavor, which changes the emitted LLVM IR parameter coercions and call signatures for certain destructor forms. The patch is accompanied by updated CodeGen tests that expect `i8*`-typed coerced `this` parameters and adjusted destructor call sites.
Mechanisms: ABI-specific computation of the implicit `this` argument type for methods/tructors; GlobalDecl-aware destructor type selection (complete vs deleting destructor); Microsoft C++ ABI virtual dispatch/vftable lookup adjustment for destructor calls; CodeGen IR signature/coercion changes for constructor/destructor emission; Member/operator call lowering now threads `GlobalDecl` through common helper logic

Risk relevance: Touches core clang codegen paths that determine destructor/method call ABI lowering; Changes how `this` is typed/coerced for destructors, which can alter generated IR and downstream optimizer assumptions; Introduces `GlobalDecl`-dependent behavior for destructor variants, increasing complexity around overload/ABI selection; Microsoft ABI virtual destructor handling is especially sensitive because deleting/base/complete destructors have different lowering rules; Any incorrect `this` typing can cascade into mismatched call signatures, invalid bitcasts, or miscompiled destructor dispatch
